clue.text: Definitive lesson in canoeing at the front

parts.note: a lesson at school is a class

indicators.note: the front of each of the words in and canoeing is taken

explanation.surface: A canoeing instructor's opening session is held up as the model one.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic version is the standard or authoritative one, which is what definitive means here.

clue.text: Conservative whip and news chief had a barney

parts.note: lash means whip
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A Tory whip and a newspaper editor had a row.
explanation.walkthrough: A barney is British slang for a noisy quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To clash is to argue or fight, which is having a row.

clue.text: Love helping to support bill by opposition leader

indicators.note: in a down clue the helping sits beneath the rest, holding it up

parts.note: an ad is a bill or poster

indicators.note: the leading letter of opposition is taken

parts.note: a ration is a portion, a helping

explanation.surface: Someone helps back a parliamentary bill drafted by the opposition leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love or worship.

clue.text: South American shopping centre is not very big

parts.note: mall is the American word for a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A South American shopping centre turns out to be modest in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one phrase, but splits after South.
explanation.definitionFit: Small means little, which is what not very big says.

clue.text: Carbon and chlorine spelt incorrectly in journal

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: the letters are spelt the wrong way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A science journal has misspelt the names of two elements.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a record of events, as is a journal; many newspapers take the name.

clue.text: Hold back substanceless reportage by reporters

indicators.note: with its substance gone, only the outer shell of the word reportage remains

parts.note: the press is the body of reporters

explanation.surface: Someone suppresses flimsy journalism produced by journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress feelings or news is to restrain or hold them back.

clue.text: One voraciously wanting to get out of head?

definitions.text: One voraciously wanting to get out of head?

parts.words: One voraciously wanting to get out of head?
parts.note: out of your head is slang for drunk or high, which a party-lover craves

explanation.surface: Someone desperate to escape their own thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is a wild partygoer who seeks to get blissfully intoxicated.

clue.text: Bud on a counter is pleasant to a taste

parts.note: bud is short for buddy, a pal
a table is a counter or flat surface

explanation.surface: A flower bud on a kitchen counter is described as tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bud' looks botanical, but it is the American word for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable food is agreeable to eat; the word comes from palate.

clue.text: The best English roofer comes from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming from the bottom means reading upward

parts.note: a tile covers a roof

explanation.surface: England's finest roofer is from the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roofer' is the tile itself, not the tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the pick of a group, the best of the bunch.

clue.text: Part of group infiltrated by old FBI agents

indicators.note: the agents get inside the group, so they sit within it

parts.note: a set is a group
G-men was the old slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: Part of a criminal group has been penetrated by federal agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a section or portion of something.

clue.text: Incense traveller saved by motor rescue company

indicators.note: the traveller is held safe within the rescue company, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British breakdown service
a Rom is a Romany, a traveller

explanation.surface: A traveller with burning incense gets rescued by the breakdown service.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, which rescues broken-down motorists. 'Incense' is the noun here, not the verb meaning anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is the sweet smell given off by burning spices, so it serves as a word for a fragrance.

clue.text: Fighting against your own state is disgusting

definitions.meaning: rising in revolt against one's own government

explanation.surface: Civil rebellion is condemned as vile.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting is both the participle of revolt, rebelling, and an adjective for something nauseating.

clue.text: Top act cruise ship put on kept snorting drug

indicators.note: the cruise ship is placed after the first part
kept takes the drug in through the nose, so the drug goes inside it

parts.note: kept means had, as in held
E is ecstasy
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A star performer on a cruise ship has been secretly taking cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the star performer at the top of the bill.

clue.text: Main idea of article chaps finally censored

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for chaps is cut out

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: The central point of an article about men was cut by the censor in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or central thread of a work.

clue.text: What will bore physician seen with sick

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A tedious doctor turns up alongside a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as making someone weary, but here it means to drill a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is the tool that bores holes.

clue.text: Keep a close eye on game king sitting on behind

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the next

parts.note: loo is an old card game
K is the chess abbreviation for king
after means behind in time or order

explanation.surface: Watching a king at play as he sits on his rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' tempts as the backside; it means after.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after something is to tend it, watching it closely.

clue.text: Knight putting new bracelet on religious type

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight places a new bracelet on a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the bracelet, but it is the anagram signal for N plus BRACELET.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrant is the priest who officiates at a service such as Mass.

clue.text: Itch to get plastered with lager as listless

indicators.note: plastered means very drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone drinks lager to forget an itch and ends up sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means lacking energy, sluggish and apathetic.

clue.text: Odd Austen novel filled with a sense of wonder

definitions.text: filled with a sense of wonder

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A strange Jane Austen novel leaves readers awestruck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book by Austen, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounded means amazed, struck with wonder.

clue.text: Tory party has 40 day period to become sympathetic

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative
a do is a party
Lent is the forty days before Easter

explanation.surface: The Conservatives hold a party, then a forty-day fast, to seem compassionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Condolent is an uncommon adjective for expressing sympathy, as in condolence.

clue.text: Chat about getting in taxi close to The Savoy?

indicators.note: the chat climbs into the taxi, so it goes inside

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: the closing letter of the is taken
turned about, so the word for chat reads backwards

parts.note: gab is idle chat

explanation.surface: A chatty passenger takes a taxi to the Savoy, the London hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy is a famous London hotel, but the definition is just 'Savoy', a crinkly-leaved cabbage; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoy is a variety of cabbage with wrinkled leaves, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Especially old paintings mounted the wrong way round

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: hung back to front, so the word for paintings reads backwards

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: Old paintings were hung upside down, especially embarrassing for a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra as an adverb means unusually, as in extra careful.

clue.text: Question chancellor about article with suspicion

indicators.note: the question and chancellor are wrapped around the article

parts.note: to ask is to question
CE is Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the Chancellor warily while questioning him about an article.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for Chancellor of the Exchequer, the UK finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to look sideways, with doubt or distrust.

clue.text: Wood block knocked over by the middle of saw

indicators.note: tipped over, so the word for block is turned back to front

parts.note: a slab is a block

indicators.note: the central letter of saw is taken

explanation.surface: A wooden block is knocked over by the saw cutting through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber used for models.

clue.text: Hebrew character going through alamedas

indicators.note: the answer runs through the inside of the word alamedas

explanation.surface: A Hebrew figure strolls along tree-lined avenues.
explanation.walkthrough: An alameda is a shaded public walk, so 'character' suggests a person walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamed is the twelfth letter of the Hebrew alphabet; a letter is a character.

clue.text: Easily secured rhino is something hunter might miss

definitions.meaning: rhino is old British slang for money, so this is money made without effort
a speedy male deer would be hard to shoot

explanation.surface: A tethered rhinoceros is an easy target that a hunter could still miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhino' is old British slang for cash, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast buck is quick, easy money; read literally, it is a swift stag.

clue.text: At work, tucking into beer is without equal

indicators.note: the working part is tucked inside the beer

parts.note: ale is beer
on means working, as in on duty

explanation.surface: Drinking beer at work, a person stands unrivalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' looks like eating or drinking, but it says one piece goes inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone can mean unique, unmatched, as in alone in his field.

clue.text: One who loves a brew is jerk that man punches

indicators.note: that man punches his way into the jerk, so he goes inside

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
he is that man

explanation.surface: A tea-lover who is a jerk is punched by another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' suggests an idiot, but it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A theic is someone who drinks tea to excess; brew is a British word for a cup of tea.

clue.text: Member meeting powerful old American high-flyer

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
strong means powerful

explanation.surface: A club member meets a mighty American achiever of years past.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong, the American astronaut, flew higher than most: he walked on the Moon.

clue.text: Nurse and academic will get back to you

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A nurse and a lecturer promise to return your call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will get back to you' looks like the promise of a reply; the definition is 'back to you', an end facing the viewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed end on has its end, its back, pointed toward the observer.

clue.text: Back, bottom or front parts of several equines

parts.note: the end is the bottom or rear

indicators.note: the leading letters of several and equines are taken

explanation.surface: A description of horses viewed from behind, beneath or in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to back or support, originally by signing on the reverse of a cheque.

clue.text: Rogue welcomed by American spies European bugs

indicators.note: the rogue is taken in by the spies, so it goes inside

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a rogue

explanation.surface: A villain is taken in by US agents spying on Europeans, who are bugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' suggests listening devices, but it means insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicadas are true bugs, insects noted for their loud chirping; cicadae is the Latin plural.
